research_role: Targeted exploratory extension for relational commitment, duty, economic dependence, and avowal under pressure. Selection does not establish any T/P/E score or comparative genre frequency.

works.title: Pengar
works.author: Victoria Benedictsson
works.selection_reason: Selma distinguishes marital vows from a declaration of felt love; chapters 5 and 6. The vow is a contextual lead, not automatically an eligible ILY occurrence.
works.source_note: Runeberg's introductory web note incorrectly describes this text as a short story in Fran Skane; the ten-chapter text is the novel Pengar. Preserve the page texts without correcting OCR or spelling.

works.title: Constance Ring
works.author: Amalie Skram
works.selection_reason: Chapter XXIV: Constance answers Lorck's demand for ILY while deliberately recovering memories of marital happiness. Prior affection makes a low-T or absent-affection interpretation an open question.
works.source_note: Use National Library of Norway public-domain first-edition scans and their OCR, independently of the Bokselskap digital edition. Historical Dano-Norwegian is coded no, consistently with Ibsen in the baseline.

works.title: The Odd Women
works.author: George Gissing
works.selection_reason: Economic dependence, courtship commitments, and demands for verbal reassurance. Chapter XVI's demand and evasion are contextual controls, not completed ILY utterances.

works.title: Vera
works.author: Elizabeth von Arnim
works.selection_reason: Chapter XVII couples Lucy's repeated ILY with private vows about her future conduct. Felt love is also present; private resolve alone need not satisfy the classifier's interpersonal commitment criterion.

works.title: Lucie
works.author: Amalie Skram
works.selection_reason: The Henny/Knut courtship scene, chapter XVII in corrected numbering, couples a declaration of love with acceptance and belonging. This is a prospective P case, not evidence of absent affection.
works.source_note: Use National Library of Norway public-domain first-edition scans and their OCR, independently of the Bokselskap digital edition. Preserve original chapter misnumbering and record it in the passage notes. Historical Dano-Norwegian is coded no, consistently with Ibsen in the baseline.
